Provenance: read from billing at 72519931c18773aacd66ff8dd942a209af10761e, from `Subscriptions::Lifecycle#payload/2` on the `customer.subscription.created` path. The commit is fleet.yml's sourceCommit for billing, and billing's tree was verifiably AT it (clean, HEAD) when this was transcribed. **RE-READ 2026-10-02 at that same commit, which is still billing's HEAD: this schema does not describe what its publisher emits.** The citation above is accurate about where the shape was looked for and wrong about the shape.

What billing emits, read out of `app/services/subscriptions/lifecycle.rb` at that commit. `core_payload/1` (line 353) writes, unconditionally, `subscription_id` (billing's own `subscriptions.id`, a bare uuid), `plan_id` (`plans.id`, a bare uuid), `account_id` (`customers.owner_id`, identity's uuid), `status` and `currency`; then `quantity` only when the processor sent an Integer, and `trial_ends_at` only while `status == "trialing"`. `payload/2` (line 350) merges `started_at` on the start path. billing asserts the resulting key set itself, in `test/services/subscriptions/lifecycle_test.rb:264-271`: `account_id currency plan_id quantity started_at status subscription_id`.

So this schema, closed with `additionalProperties: false`, **rejects four fields every real start carries** (`plan_id`, `account_id`, `currency`, `started_at`) and **requires four it never receives** (`processor`, `processor_event_id`, `kind`, `customer_id`). billing knows both halves and has said so in its own source for some time: `PENDING_PAYLOAD_ALIGNMENT` in `test/contract/outbox_envelope_contract_test.rb:76-79` lists exactly these as `unexpected` and `missing` and is asserted in both directions, and `lifecycle.rb:320-343` records that core's schemas "describe a different payload, and this is recorded rather than matched" and that "when core decides, the change lands here and in the contract test together".

**Why the transcription went stale rather than being wrong when written.** D10 rewrote this schema because billing had no subscriptions table, which was true of billing-03b and stopped being true when `db/migrate/20260930000007_create_subscriptions.rb` landed (`id: :uuid, default: -> { "gen_random_uuid()" }`) — and `plans` and `customers` were uuid tables before that. A payload schema describes what a publisher emits (docs/event-naming.md), so the honest reading is that this file is behind its publisher and core owes it a rewrite. D39 records why that rewrite is **not** in this commit, what it costs, and what flipping it looks like; the short form is that applying it deletes four properties this schema has required since v0.2, on a contract one publisher has already documented as knowingly divergent and is waiting on core to move. That is a manager-owned call with consumer consequences, and it is not made silently in a packet about three disagreements. **What is not in dispute and is fixed here is the claim in this repository that billing has no such fields** — examples/invalid/README.md, docs/event-naming.md and this file all said it, and all three are corrected in the same commit.
title: billing.subscription.started payload
description: The `data` payload of the `billing.subscription.started` event: a subscription became active. A trial counts as started, which is why `status` carries the distinction rather than the type name. The payload is normalised from a payment processor's own webhook, so the ids are the processor's (`sub_…`, `cus_…`, `price_…`) and `processor`/`processor_event_id` say where the fact came from — a consumer must be able to tell a fact billing knows from a fact billing was told. **This schema does not describe what its publisher emits, and the disagreement is in both directions.** billing has a `subscriptions` table and emits `subscription_id`, `plan_id`, `account_id`, `status`, `currency`, `quantity` and `started_at` — all bare uuids, no cafaye prefix anywhere — and emits none of the `processor`/`processor_event_id`/`kind`/`customer_id` this file requires; the exact emitted key set, the source lines, the commit, and billing's own two-way record of the gap are in this file's `$comment`. So **a real `billing.subscription.started` does not validate against this schema**, and it did not start doing so by accident of a value: billing grew the table D10 said it did not have. See [D10](../DECISIONS.md#d10-billingsubscriptionstarteds-payload-schema-no-longer-describes-cafaye-ids) for the decision that is right and stale, and [D39](../DECISIONS.md#d39-does-a-payload-schema-follow-its-publisher-when-the-publisher-has-grown-the-feature-the-schema-predicted-it-would-not) for the one that is open. The envelope is validated by schemas/event-envelope.schema.json; this schema validates what is inside `data`. The file path is the event type with dots as directory separators. See docs/event-naming.md.

processor.description: The payment processor this subscription lives at. Present on every billing payload: an id from a processor means nothing without knowing which processor issued it, and a second processor is not a hypothetical.

processor_event_id.description: The processor's own event id for the webhook this came from, e.g. `evt_…`. The deduplication key for the ingestion, and the only way to trace a payload back to the fact it records.

kind.description: Always `subscription`. The three subscription events share one normaliser, and this is what tells a consumer which family of payload it is looking at without reading the envelope's type.

subscription_id.description: The processor's subscription id, e.g. `sub_…`. Always equal to the envelope's `subject` for this event. It is the processor's id, not a cafaye one — see D10.

customer_id.description: The processor's customer id, e.g. `cus_…`. The join back to a `billing.customer.created`, whose `processor_customer_id` is the same value. This is how a subscription event reaches an account without a subscriptions table.

status.description: The subscription's status as the processor reports it — `active`, `trialing`, `past_due`, `canceled` and whatever else it grows. Deliberately not an enum here: it is a third party's vocabulary, and core freezing it would make every processor addition a spec release. Read `trialing` for a subscription that started on a trial.

quantity.description: Units billed for, or null when the subscription carries no quantity. Seats on a per-seat plan, units on a metered one.

price_id.description: The processor's price id, e.g. `price_…`, or null. On a `billing.plan.created` payload the same value is called `processor_price_id`; the two names are the two sides' own.

unit_amount.description: Price per unit, as integer minor units and a currency — or null when the processor sent neither. Null is not zero: a missing price is missing, and defaulting it is how a customer ends up on a plan nobody charged them for.

amount_minor.description: Per-unit amount in the currency's minor units.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code, uppercase — normalised on the way in, because a processor that sends `usd` and one that sends `USD` are describing the same currency.

current_period_start.description: RFC3339 UTC when the current billing period began, or null when the processor sent no timestamp. A missing timestamp is not the epoch.

current_period_end.description: RFC3339 UTC when the current billing period ends. This is when a `cancel_at_period_end` cancellation takes effect.

cancel_at_period_end.description: Whether the subscription is set to stop at the end of the period. False is not the same as null: false is a decision, null is the absence of one.

canceled_at.description: RFC3339 UTC when the subscription was cancelled, or null while it has not been. Null on every `billing.subscription.started`.

trial.description: Whether the subscription has a trial. The boolean form of what `status: trialing` says, and unlike `status` it cannot be null — the publisher derives it.
